thread:
alina: Heads-up — we saw a regression on prod llm-13b (chat template workloads). Latency up ~18% on median for short-turn chats. Posting quick profiler dump and initial hypotheses.

mike: Oof. When did this start?

alina: Started around the 3340000000 deploy window. Perf-bot flagged increased p50 during canary.

perf-bot: alert: p50 latency increased from 42ms -> 50ms on /generate (llm-13b, default rope_theta). trace_id=trk_334a

jorge: Any kernel switch in the logs? Kernel selector can flip to the slow NV fused path if shapes/strides look non-optimal.

alina: That's my suspicion. I attached a short profiling snippet:
```
# sample from perf trace (single request)
model: llm-13b
hidden: 8192
heads: 64
rope_theta: default (auto)
sequence: 32 -> 64 (chatpad)
kernel chosen: matmul_scalar_loop (fallback)
matmul time: 18.4ms (was 10.2ms before)
KV copy/evict: 3.1ms (unchanged)
context build: 6.2ms
```

sasha: matmul_scalar_loop is our slow path. Why did selector pick it? Could be stride mismatch from chat template padding + kv layout change.

mike: Did anyone change the rope_theta defaults? We recently landed a change that adjusts rope scaling heuristics per head dim — could be interacting.

alina: Yes, PR #1248 altered rope_theta auto-scaling for 64-head configs (trying to reduce numeric drift). That PR landed in the same window.

rachel: Note: the chat template adds a 128-token system prompt pad that causes the runtime to see a 160-seq hot path even for short user turns, so kernel selector may see longer seq distribution and pick different kernels.

jorge: So two interacting signals: rope_theta change affects kernel heuristics (we compute token scaling for rope-based kernels) + observed sequence length profile shifts from chatpad. Selector heuristics weight both. That's plausible.

alina: Quick repro on staging: toggle rope_theta to fixed 10000 vs auto. With fixed 10000, kernel selector picks fused_matmul and matmul time returns to ~10.8ms. With auto, we see fallback.

mike: Interesting. Any difference in output quality? We need to make sure this isn't a correctness fix.

alina: No diffs on a small eval prompt set. Numeric alignment is within epsilon. This looks like a performance-only regression.

rachel: Short term mitigation: pin rope_theta to 10000 for llm-13b chat template routes, and force kernel preference to fused_matmul in the route config. That should be safe until we tune selector.

jorge: Also adjust batching heuristic: if chat_template.pad_tokens > 100, treat user turn length distribution as short-tail and cap batch.max_seq to 64 to avoid selector overfitting to padded length.

mike: Agree. Can we implement a minimal config override in the router by EOD? Who owns?

alina: I can push the route change (pin rope_theta + kernel_pref) and add a temporary feature flag. Will open PR against routing-config.

sasha: I'll start an investigation branch to reproduce selector decision tree and add instrumentation to log the selector scoring vector (weights for seq_len, head_dim, rope_scale). Need that to prevent future surprises.

perf-bot: note: created issue perf/334000 on perf dashboard linking the trace and canary graphs.

rachel: Postmortem/next steps: 1) short-term route override (alina) 2) selector scoring telemetry (sasha) 3) revert/adjust rope_theta autotune PR if needed (owner mike) 4) update batching heuristic for chatpad detection (jorge).

mike: I'll own the rope_theta PR rollback/adjust. If we can get the route override in and tests green, roll it to prod and monitor.

alina: PR: routing-config#332 filed, force pin and kernel pref. Will post link once CI finishes.

sasha: For the selector instrumentation, I'll add a lightweight log line: 
`selector.debug: {model, head_dim, rope_theta, seq_hint, score_fused, score_scalar}`
so we can correlate with traces.

jorge: Also check KV cache alignment; I saw small extra memcpy when kernel switched. Might be due to different expected stride for head-kv layout. I'll add a microbenchmark for kv-load/store stride 64 vs 128 to confirm.

alina: Thanks all. If we can get the override in next 2 hours we can avoid more user impact. I'll ping #oncall if latency creeps up. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks, team. Keep updates brief here and post links to PRs/traces.
